Written for the reference couple owning the wealth 50/50 and taxed separately: per person the tax-free amount of net wealth is 2,000,000 (allowance as the regional rule, ITSGF band where it governs) + 300,000 (main home, art. 4.Nueve LIP) = 2,300,000, so 4,600,000 for the couple, and every bracket limit is doubled. The engine passes net wealth including the home, so the home exemption is folded into the allowance. wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax (IBI, roughly 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value) and the municipal land-value gain tax on sales (IIVTNU) are ordinary local taxes and are not modelled as wealth tax.

income_cap.notes: Art. 31 Ley 19/1991 (and art. 3.Doce Ley 38/2022 for the ITSGF): the IRPF cuota on the general and savings bases plus wealth tax may not exceed 60% of the IRPF taxable base, leaving out gains on assets held over a year; the wealth tax is cut to fit, by at most 80%. Applied per spouse; with a 50/50 split the couple's figures are twice one spouse's.

inheritance.summary: Valencia: EUR 100,000 reduction and 99% rebate for children on inheritances and gifts (since 28/5/2023); about 0.33% of a EUR 10m inheritance.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Group II reduction EUR 100,000 (art. 10 Ley 13/1997, as amended by Ley 5/2026); regional scale top 34% above EUR 781,916.75; multipliers 1.0-1.2.

Scored for the reference couple (each spouse taxed separately; tax-free amount EUR 800,000 per person, EUR 1,600,000 for the couple), net wealth including the home: EUR 10m: EUR 85,128; EUR 20m: EUR 248,159; EUR 35m: EUR 714,228, before the joint IRPF limit.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Allowance EUR 550,000 per person (art. 28.1 LF 13/1992); main home exempt up to EUR 250,000 per person (art. 5.7). Joint limit with IRPF (art. 31): IRPF + IP at most 65% of the IRPF base (gains on assets held over a year in the savings base excluded), but the IP reduction is capped at 55%; limits are computed per person even for a family unit.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: The 3.5% top band (above EUR 11,003,784.50 of base) is set year by year in DA 1ª LF 13/1992; Ley Foral 17/2025 (BON 31/12/2025) re-enacted the same scale for the 2026 tax period. It replaces the state ITSGF for Navarra residents and would need re-enacting for 2027.

components.name: Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio de Navarra, married couple owning 50/50
components.notes: Navarra's own scale (LF 13/1992 art. 30 and DA 1ª for 2026, re-enacted by Ley Foral 17/2025): 0.16% rising to 2.0%, and 3.5% above EUR 11,003,784.50 of taxable base. There is no ITSGF in Navarra (Convenio Económico) and no general rebate, so the scale is the whole tax. The tax is individual (art. 2, 6 and 7 LF 13/1992; assets common to both spouses are attributed half to each unless another share is shown). Written for the reference couple owning the wealth 50/50: per person the tax-free amount is 550,000 (mínimo exento, art. 28.1) + 250,000 (main home, art. 5.7) = 800,000, so 1,600,000 for the couple, and every bracket limit is doubled (single limits 155,511.88; 311,023.76; 622,047.53; 1,244,095.06; 2,488,190.11; 4,976,380.22; 9,952,760.45; 11,003,784.50). The engine passes net wealth including the home, so the home exemption is folded into the allowance. The joint IRPF limit (art. 31 LF 13/1992: 65%, reduction at most 55%) is modelled in income_cap.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax (IBI, roughly 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value) and the municipal land-value gain tax on sales (IIVTNU) are ordinary local taxes and are not modelled as wealth tax.

income_cap.notes: Art. 31 LF 13/1992: IRPF cuota plus IP cuota may not exceed 65% of the IRPF taxable base (leaving out the savings-base balance of gains on assets held more than a year, and the part of the IP on assets that yield no taxable income); the IP is cut to fit, by at most 55% (at least 45% stays due). Computed per person even for a family unit (art. 31.3). Applied per spouse; with a 50/50 split the couple's figures are twice one spouse's.

inheritance.summary: Navarra: children (any age) pay 0% on the first EUR 250,000 of taxable base and then 2%, 4%, 8%, 12% and 16% above EUR 3m; about 13.53% of a EUR 10m inheritance.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Art. 34.1.a.3º DFL 250/2002: progressive scale for descendants; no separate parent-child allowance (the 0% first band acts as one).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Navarra law applies to inheritances when the deceased was habitually resident in Navarra (art. 31 Convenio Económico).

inheritance.spouse_note: Spouses and stable partners pay 0% on the first EUR 250,000 of taxable base and a flat 0.8% on the rest for inheritances (art. 34.1.a.1º DFL 250/2002), about 0.8% of a large estate, against up to 16% for children.
inheritance.gift_tax: Gifts to children: 0.8% to EUR 250,000, 2% to 500,000, 3% to 1m, 4% to 1.8m, 6% to 3m, 8% above (art. 34.1.a.4º): about 7.4% on a EUR 10m gift.
inheritance.business_relief: Navarra has its own family-business reliefs (not researched in detail).
inheritance.foreign_assets: Resident heirs are taxed on worldwide acquisitions, with credit for foreign inheritance tax.
inheritance.domicile_rules: Regional rules apply to inheritances when the deceased spent most days of the last 5 years in this region (art. 28 Ley 22/2009) and to gifts of movable assets when the donee did; otherwise state or another region's rules apply. Non-resident heirs may also use them (DA 2ª Ley 29/1987).

units.summary: Basque Country (foral regime, three territories with own taxes; numbers modelled on Bizkaia): savings income 19-28%; wealth tax from EUR 800,000 at 0.2%-2%, foral ITSGF only at the top; children's inheritances: EUR 400,000 allowance then a flat 1.5% (Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa), gifts 1.5% from the first euro. Foral rules apply to arrivals from abroad at once, but not if the deceased/donee spent more of the last 5 years in common-regime Spain. The state Beckham regime does not apply.

capital_gains.summary: The Basque Country has its own IRPF per territory; from 1 January 2026 Álava, Bizkaia and Gipuzkoa apply the same savings scale, 19% to 28% (28% above EUR 300,000).
capital_gains.regional_differences: The three territories legislate separately, but NF 2/2025 (Bizkaia), NF 3/2025 (Álava) and NF 1/2025 (Gipuzkoa) adopted the same savings scale with effect from 1 January 2026 (Cuatrecasas, May 2025); Bizkaia's consolidated text was checked directly.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Basque impatriate regime instead of the state Beckham regime.

wealth_tax.summary: Basque Country (modelled on Bizkaia): own wealth tax, EUR 800,000 allowance and main home exempt up to EUR 400,000 per person, 0.2%-2.0%; the foral solidarity tax (NF 9/2023, 800,000 allowance, 1.5%-3.5%) tops it up only at the very top. Scored for the reference couple (each spouse taxed separately; tax-free amount EUR 1,200,000 per person, EUR 2,400,000 for the couple), net wealth including the home: EUR 10m: EUR 62,800; EUR 20m: EUR 224,800; EUR 35m: EUR 514,000, before the joint IRPF limit.
wealth_tax.exemptions_thresholds: Bizkaia, per person: allowance EUR 800,000; main home exempt up to EUR 400,000; joint limit with IRPF 65% of the general and savings bases, IP reduction capped at 75% (art. 33 NF 2/2013).
wealth_tax.regional_differences: Bizkaia is modelled. Per Guía Fiscal (secondary source, updated 29/07/2026): Álava (NF 9/2013, revised by NF 3/2025) has the same EUR 800,000 allowance and EUR 400,000 main-home exemption but its own 8-band scale topping out at 2.5%; Gipuzkoa (NF 2/2018, revised by NF 1/2025) has a EUR 700,000 allowance, EUR 300,000 main-home exemption and a 2.5% top rate. Each territory has its own foral solidarity tax (Bizkaia NF 9/2023, Gipuzkoa NF 3/2023, Álava NF 23/2023) for net wealth above EUR 3m, credited against the foral IP. So Álava and Gipuzkoa are somewhat more expensive than the modelled Bizkaia figures at high wealth.
wealth_tax.important_exceptions: The ITSGF is a concerted tax with foral rules (Concierto DA 5ª); each territory adopted its own norm (Bizkaia NF 9/2023).

components.name: Impuesto sobre el Patrimonio de Bizkaia / foral ITSGF, married couple owning 50/50
components.notes: Modelled on Bizkaia (NF 2/2013): mínimo exento 800,000, scale 0.2% to 2.0%; the foral solidarity tax (NF 9/2023, net wealth above EUR 3m, credited against the foral IP) takes over only at the very top (3.5% band). The state ITSGF does not apply in the foral territories (Concierto Económico). Written for the reference couple owning the wealth 50/50 and taxed separately: per person the tax-free amount is 800,000 (mínimo exento) + 400,000 (main home exempt up to EUR 400,000, art. 5 NF 2/2013) = 1,200,000, so 2,400,000 for the couple, and every bracket limit is doubled (single limits 800,000; 1,600,000; 3,200,000; 6,400,000; 12,800,000; 15,993,333.33). The engine passes net wealth including the home, so the home exemption is folded into the allowance. The joint IRPF limit (art. 33 NF 2/2013: 65%, reduction at most 75%) is modelled in income_cap.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Municipal real estate tax (IBI, roughly 0.4-1.1% of cadastral value) and the municipal land-value gain tax on sales (IIVTNU) are ordinary local taxes and are not modelled as wealth tax.

income_cap.notes: Bizkaia, art. 33 NF 2/2013 ('escudo fiscal'): IRPF cuota plus IP cuota may not exceed 65% of the IRPF general and savings bases; the IP is cut to fit, by at most 75%. Whether gains on assets held over a year are left out of the base (as in the state and Navarra rules) was not confirmed, so false is an assumption. Gipuzkoa and Álava limits were not researched. Applied per spouse; with a 50/50 split the couple's figures are twice one spouse's.

inheritance.summary: Basque Country: Group I (children of any age, spouse, parents) gets a EUR 400,000 reduction on inheritances and pays a flat 1.5% above it (Bizkaia NF 4/2015 arts. 43, 47; same in Gipuzkoa); about 1.44% of a EUR 10m inheritance.
inheritance.exemptions_thresholds: Reduction EUR 400,000 per Group I heir; flat 1.5% (Bizkaia art. 47; Gipuzkoa from 16/05/2025 reductions sheet).
inheritance.important_exceptions: Concierto art. 25.Dos: Basque rules are replaced by common-regime rules when the deceased (inheritance) or donee (gift) spent more days of the last 5 years in common-regime Spain; years abroad do not trigger this.
